subject.title: [Bug]: Slack inbound wedge after context overflow/compaction; Socket Mode remains connected but replies stop

question: After an unrecoverable compaction failure on a queued channel session, should OpenClaw automatically archive-and-rotate that exact session for the next inbound message, or require an explicit user/operator reset?
rationale: The existing recovery work handles stale active-run liveness, but the proposed remedy changes the user-facing session continuity and retention policy after a terminal compaction failure.

options.title: Archive and rotate automatically
options.body: On a confirmed terminal compaction outcome, retain the old transcript as an archive, release the lane, and create a fresh session for the next inbound message with a clear notice.

options.title: Require explicit reset
options.body: Keep the session intact and surface a channel action or command that the user or operator must invoke to create a fresh session.

options.title: Add only diagnostics first
options.body: Collect a narrowed Slack/Codex repro and terminal outcome telemetry before committing to any automatic session-rotation behavior.

recommendation.title: Archive and rotate automatically
recommendation.body: On a confirmed terminal compaction outcome, retain the old transcript as an archive, release the lane, and create a fresh session for the next inbound message with a clear notice.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Codex compaction ownership and persisted session-recovery behavior addressed by their related merged work.
